---
title: "Model viewer"
---

The [Model viewer](../viewer.qmd) shows the input and results of the coupled LHM model (`lhm_coupled`) of `main` on a web map.
It is a static web app: the docs site serves only the JavaScript, and the browser reads the model data directly from MinIO.
The model of a pull request can be previewed too, together with its differences from `main`, at `https://ribasim.nl/viewer?pr=<number>`.
Any other published version can be viewed, or compared with another, by its commit, see [Links to a version](#links-to-a-version).

The *Water authority* choice above the layer list shows the nodes and links of one authority, by the `waterbeheercode` their node ids start with, see `ribasim_nl.aquo`.
It also shows the links to other authorities and the nodes at their other end, such as the regional inlets and outlets of the hws, and the Basin / areas of the shown Basins.
The choice is kept in the URL, as `#authority=<waterbeheercode>`.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[modellen/lhm_coupled] -->|dvc repro run_lhm_coupled| R[runs/lhm_coupled]
  R -->|dvc repro export_webmap| B[webmap/lhm_coupled]
  B -->|pixi run publish-webmap| C[MinIO doc-image/webmap]
  C --> D[Model viewer page]
  L[dvc.lock on GitHub main] --> D
```

All local paths are relative to `data/Rijkswaterstaat`.

## Fit to the measurements

The *Observations* choice in the time bar colors the Observation nodes by how well the simulated values fit their measurements, see `ribasim_nl.goodness_of_fit`:

- *KGE* and *NSE*: the Kling-Gupta and Nash-Sutcliffe efficiencies over the whole run, from purple at -1 to green at 1. At 0 the results are as good as the mean of the measurements.
- *bias*: the difference of the mean simulated and measured value, relative to the mean absolute measurement. It is green within 25%, the limit of a satisfactory bias of discharges of Moriasi et al. (2007), grey at 50%, and purple from 100% either way.
- *simulated − observed*: the difference at the time of the time bar, from red for too low to blue for too high. It is colored on a symmetric log scale, since the differences of large rivers and small ditches span orders of magnitude.

The efficiencies and bias need 365 days with both a measured and a simulated value, so Observation nodes with fewer days, or without a measurement at the time of the time bar, are small grey dots.
Change the limits of a color scale in its legend.
The *Observations* box above the layer list lists the shown Observation nodes by their fit, the best or the worst first, with the median, and zooms to one when clicked.
The panel of an Observation node shows its fit above the chart of its observed and simulated values.

## Updating the published data

1. Run the model with the `run_lhm_coupled` DVC stage.
    It copies the model of `modellen/lhm_coupled` to `runs/lhm_coupled`, and writes the results next to it.
    It also writes the commit of the code to `runinfo.json`, which the viewer shows next to the scale bar, with the time the run finished from `results/ribasim.log`.
    For now this runs with a looser solver tolerance, see `pipeline/run_lhm_coupled.py`.
    The NetCDF results are compressed, to save space in DVC.
    This takes many hours, so normally pull the cached results instead:

    ```sh
    pixi run dvc pull run_lhm_coupled
    ```

2. Export the model to web-friendly files with the `export_webmap` DVC stage, which takes about 10 minutes:

    ```sh
    pixi run dvc repro --pull --single-item export_webmap
    ```

    This writes `data/Rijkswaterstaat/webmap/lhm_coupled`, see `ribasim_nl.webmap` for details:

    | File | Content |
    |:-----|:--------|
    | `nodes.parquet` | Node table with all attributes and lon/lat |
    | `links.parquet` | Link table with all attributes and simplified geometry |
    | `basin_area.pmtiles` | Basin / area polygons as vector tiles |
    | `waterboards.geojson` | Simplified water board boundaries |
    | `tables/*.parquet` | All other input tables, including those in NetCDF, sorted by `node_id` |
    | `results/*_by_id.parquet` | Basin and flow results sorted by id, for the time series charts |
    | `results/*_by_time.parquet` | Basin level and storage, and flow rate, ordered by time step, for coloring the map |
    | `results/observation_metrics.parquet` | How well the results fit the measurements of each Observation node, see [Fit to the measurements](#fit-to-the-measurements) |
    | `results/observation_by_time.parquet` | The difference simulated − observed of each Observation node, ordered by time step, for coloring the map |
    | `manifest.json` | List of the files above with their content hash and size, the color scale of each result variable, and when and from which commit the model was run |

    Results are only exported if the model's `results` directory exists.
    DVC does not cache this output, since the published model on MinIO is a copy of it already.
    `dvc.lock` does record its hash, which names the published model.

3. Push the run and commit the updated `dvc.lock`, see [DVC](dvc.qmd#pushing-changes):

    ```sh
    pixi run dvc push run_lhm_coupled
    ```

4. Publish the model as a preview of the pull request of the current branch.
    This needs credentials with write access in `.env`, and the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) `gh`, logged in.

    ```sh
    pixi run publish-webmap
    ```

    This uploads the model of the working tree, and that of `origin/main`, which it fetches first, and their differences, see [Comparing models](#comparing-models).
    It then adds a comment to the pull request with the link `https://ribasim.nl/viewer?pr=<number>` and a summary of the differences, or updates that comment on later publishes.
    Use `--pr <number>` to publish for another pull request, and `--main` to only publish the model of `origin/main`.
    Use `--commit <revision>` to publish the model of a commit on GitHub, and add `--base <revision>` to also publish its differences from another commit, see [Links to a version](#links-to-a-version).

`pixi run repro-local` runs steps 1 to 4 by default, see [Running locally](local.qmd).
The docs do not need to be rebuilt to show another model.

### How the published models are found

Everything is uploaded to the anonymously readable `doc-image/webmap/` prefix on MinIO, see `ribasim_nl.webmap_publish`:

| Object | Content |
|:-------|:--------|
| `files/<hash>.<ext>` | The exported files, named by their content hash, so unchanged files are uploaded once and shared by all models |
| `lhm_coupled/snapshots/<md5>/manifest.json` | The manifest of an export, named by the DVC hash of the `export_webmap` output in `dvc.lock` |
| `lhm_coupled/main.json` | The snapshot of the latest published `main` |
| `lhm_coupled/diffs/<base md5>-<head md5>.json` | The differences between two snapshots |
| `lhm_coupled/prs/<number>.json` | The snapshots of a pull request and the `main` it was compared with, and their differences |

To show `main`, the viewer reads `dvc.lock` from `main` on GitHub, and loads the snapshot of its `export_webmap` output.
So once a pull request whose model was published is merged, the viewer shows its model, without publishing again.
If that snapshot is not published, for instance because a pull request changed the model without publishing it, the viewer shows the snapshot in `main.json` with a warning.
The next `pixi run publish-webmap` then exports the run of `main` again, and publishes it.
Likewise, to compare a pull request with `main`, the export of `main` is downloaded from its snapshot, or exported again from its run if it is not published.
For a pull request, the viewer warns if `main` changed since the model was published; publish again to compare with the latest `main`.
Snapshots and files that are no longer used are not deleted.

### Links to a version

Node and link IDs change between versions of the model, so a link to a node in an issue would show another node later.
The viewer therefore puts the commit of the model it shows in the page URL, so a copied link keeps showing that version:

| URL | Model |
|:----|:------|
| `viewer` | The latest `main`, then pinned to `viewer?commit=<commit>` |
| `viewer?commit=<commit>` | The model of a commit on GitHub, by the snapshot in its `dvc.lock` |
| `viewer?base=<commit>&commit=<commit>` | The model of a commit, compared with that of another commit |
| `viewer?pr=<number>` | The latest published model of a pull request, compared with its base |
| `&compare=0` | Added to a comparison: only the model, without its comparison |

Commits may be shortened; pinned links use 10 characters.
The view and selection after `#` are kept.
If a pinned model is no longer that of the latest `main`, the viewer says so, with a link to the latest `main` at the same place.
The viewer knows the commit of `main` since the docs are built and published for each push to `main`, so after a merge it shows the previous `main` until that is done.
Links to a pull request are not pinned, since it is usually published before its `dvc.lock` is committed.

Two commits can be compared if their differences are published, for instance to see what changed in a month.
Since snapshots and differences are named by the DVC hashes of the models, any two commits with the models of a published comparison can be compared, like `main` before and after a pull request.
To compare other commits, publish their models and differences:

```sh
pixi run publish-webmap --commit origin/main --base <commit>
```

This prints the link to the comparison.
A model that is not published is exported again from its run in DVC.

## Viewing local models

The viewer can also show any local model, without publishing it:

```sh
pixi run viewer data/Rijkswaterstaat/modellen/hws_2025_10_1/hws.toml
```

This exports the model with `ribasim_nl.webmap` to `.cache/viewer`, serves it with the viewer on <http://localhost:8000>, and opens it in a web browser.
The export is reused as long as the model, its results and the export code are unchanged, so only the first run takes long; about 10 minutes for the coupled LHM model with results.
Results are shown if the model's results directory exists.
Use `--port` to serve on another port, and `--no-browser` to not open a browser.

### Comparing models

To review a pull request that changes a model, view only the differences from another version of the model.
Usually that is the same model at another git revision, like `main`:

```sh
pixi run viewer data/Rijkswaterstaat/runs/lhm_coupled/lhm_coupled.toml --base origin/main
```

`--base` takes a git revision or the TOML of another model.
The model at a revision is read with DVC, from the DVC cache or the DVC remote, into `.cache/viewer/revisions`.
Add `--rev` to also take the viewed model from a git revision instead of the working tree, for instance `--rev HEAD --base origin/main`.
Fetch first to compare with the latest `origin/main`.

Nodes are matched by id, and links by their from and to node, since links get renumbered, see `ribasim_nl.webmap_diff`.
A node or link in both models is changed if its geometry, an attribute, its rows in an input table, or its Basin / area differ.
Initial Basin levels in `Basin / state` that differ less than 1 cm are equal, since every run of the regional models changes them slightly, see `TABLE_TOLERANCES` in `ribasim_nl.webmap_diff`.
The map shows only the added, removed and changed features, in the colors of their status: green, orange and purple, on a grey base map.
When zoomed out, the status rings around changed nodes become small dots.
Removed and changed Basin / areas of the old model are drawn as dashed outlines.
Turn on *Unchanged* in the layer list to show the other features faintly, for context.
Observation nodes and their links are always shown, also when unchanged or filtered out in the *Differences* box, so their charts can be compared; the observed values are charted with the simulated values of both models.
The simulated values of the base model are those of the observed node in the base model, also if its links were renumbered or lead to renumbered nodes.

If both models have results, the Basin levels and flow rates are compared too.
Basins and flow links whose results differ more than a tolerance are also shown, in shades of grey by the largest difference.
Differences of up to 1 mm in level, and of up to 1 L/s plus 1% in flow rate, are ignored as solver noise.

The *Differences* box counts the differences by status and by what changed, for instance `Basin / state` or `geometry`.
Its *View without differences* link shows the model normally, at the same place, by adding `&compare=0` to the URL.
Uncheck a status or a change to hide those features from the map, for instance to look past the many changed initial states.
It also lists the changed TOML settings, all differing features, and the features whose results differ, largest first; click one to zoom to it.
The panel of a changed feature lists what changed, shows the old value of changed attributes struck through, and shows both versions of changed tables.
The result charts show the old model as dashed lines in a lighter tint.

If both models have the fit to the measurements, the time bar has the *Observations* choice only, which can also color the Observation nodes by the change of their KGE, NSE or absolute bias, from purple for a worse to green for a better fit.
The panel of an Observation node shows the fit of both models.

## Developing the viewer

The viewer lives in [`viewer/`](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/tree/main/viewer) and is written in TypeScript, built with [Vite](https://vite.dev/).
It uses [MapLibre GL JS](https://maplibre.org/) for the basemap and the Basin / area tiles, [deck.gl](https://deck.gl/) to draw the nodes and links, and [hyparquet](https://github.com/hyparam/hyparquet) to read Parquet files with HTTP range requests.

Start a development server that serves your local `export_webmap` output, and open <http://localhost:5173>:

```sh
pixi run viewer-dev
```

Changes to the TypeScript code reload the page automatically.
`pixi run viewer-build` checks types and builds the viewer into `docs/viewer-app`.
`pixi run docs` and `pixi run docs-render` run it before rendering the docs.
Add `?data=<url>` to the viewer page URL to load the data from another location, and `&base_data=<url>&diff=<url>` to compare it with another model, for instance `?data=http://localhost:5173/` to use the development server.
Only the default MinIO host, the docs site itself and `localhost` are accepted.
